newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler to boost truck capacity in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler to boost truck capacity in 1997.

text.p: Chrysler Corp Chief Financial Officer Gary Valade said the automaker will add 190,000 vehicles worth of new truck assembly capacity next year, including production of a new Dodge sport/utility vehicle in Newark, Del.

Valade told reporters in a conference call that the capacity additions also include an increase in assembly line speed at Chrysler's St. Louis North that will allow the facility to produce an additional 20,000 Dodge Ram pickup trucks per year.

Valade said the new sport/utility at Newark, coupled with other enhancements to plants that build the Dodge Dakota pickup truck, Jeep Wrangler and Jeep Cherokee, will add 155,000 units of additional annual capacity.

In addition, Chrysler will add a third shift next year to its Eurostar joint venture plant in Graz, Austria, allowing the production of an additional 15,000 minivans and sport/utility vehicles per year. Chrysler jointly owns the plant with Steyr-Daimler-Puch AG.

The Newark-built vehicle is expected to be base on Chrysler's all-new Dodge Dakota pickup truck. The four-door vehicle will give Dodge dealers their first sport/utility vehicle since the two-door Ram Charger was discontinued several years ago.
Valade said the additional truck capacity will help Chrysler to spread its fixed costs over more vehicles, which should help the automaker's profitability.
"We can get a few more pieces out there," he added.
